title: FW: LI-2026-0142 Centrifuge Log Photo

fields.cc: Prof. Dennis Okafor (IBC Chair); Joel Whitcomb (Director of Research Compliance)
fields.subject: FW: LI-2026-0142 centrifuge log photo
fields.note:
Forwarding what I sent Dr. Anika Rao a few minutes ago so everyone has the same picture.

The photo shows the maintenance log taped to the side of the centrifuge in the shared room on three. The last vendor rotor inspection entry is 14 Aug 2025, and the sticker says "next due Aug 2026". So the inspection is overdue by a few months.

I looked through the door window only and did not go in. The room is still closed and the lid has not been opened.

Joel Whitcomb, I've copied you because this centrifuge was bought on the Iowa Corn Growers Board award. Does that change anything for the sponsor? I don't know what their award terms say about incidents.

Tell me if you need anything else from our side.
fields.signature:
Maya
Laboratory Manager, Bacterial Genetics Laboratory
Lindgren Life Sciences, 3rd floor
Halvorsen State University

original.subject: LI-2026-0142 centrifuge log photo
original.body:
Sent from my phone at the centrifuge room door.

The maintenance log on the unit shows the last vendor rotor inspection on 14 Aug 2025. The sticker says next due Aug 2026, so it's overdue.

Through the window I can see the bucket in the failed position. The sealed lid looks like it's seated crooked. There's a film on the inside of the chamber window. I can't tell whether it stayed inside the bucket or got into the chamber.

I haven't opened anything. The door is closed and I've put a sign on it. Our grad student is still in our office.

Maya

instructorNote: This clue shows that containment inside the rotor is unverified and the vendor inspection is overdue. It also brings the sponsor into the incident through the equipment purchase. Watch whether the BSO keeps the chamber sealed and records that containment is unverified. The IBC chair should start a classification note that flags a possible earlier-than-30-day report but should not decide the classification yet. The Director of Research Compliance should put LI-2026-0142 on the clock board and pull the Iowa Corn Growers Board award's incident-notice term rather than guessing at it.
